terms.grammar: noun, third declension, masculine or feminine
evidence: Phaedr. 3.13.3: līs ad forum dēducta est, vespā jūdice
Traupman 195: jūs dīcere, to sit as judge
terms.comment: In a Roman civil case the jūdex was a private citizen appointed to try it; in modern Latin any judge (Traupman 195). To sit as judge is jūs dīcere (Traupman 195, 335). Also anyone who judges, a critic: quālēs sītis jūdicēs! (Phaedr. 5.5.38). For the judge of a game see referee.

terms.gloss: the presiding judge of a criminal court
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: an examiner, an inquisitor; especially the praetor who presided in criminal trials.

phrases.latin: apēs in altā fēcerant quercū favōs: hōs fūcī inertēs esse dīcēbant suōs. līs ad forum dēducta est, vespā jūdice.
phrases.english: Bees had made their honeycombs in a tall oak; lazy drones said the combs were theirs. The dispute went to court, with a wasp as judge.

phrases.latin: grammaticī certant et adhūc sub jūdice līs est
phrases.english: the scholars disagree, and the case is still before the judge

phrases.latin: ēn hic dēclārat quālēs sītis jūdicēs!
phrases.english: Look, this shows what sort of judges you are!
